Supersedes the original scoring, which was done when all twelve cards were recorded stacked at one coordinate and could only be matched by DOM order.
_whyRescored: The pinned fix re-measures scroll-driven sections after their animation completes and re-expresses them against the sticky viewport. For this section that took the 24 card/image elements from 2 distinct positions to 24, and the section height from 3,150px (scroll distance) to 900px (visual), dropping the design/page height ratio from 4.93x to 1.41x. Element COUNTS were unchanged at 34/36, but reading order changed completely, so every web index in the previous file pointed at a different element. Counts are not sufficient to validate index stability - element identity must be checked.
_truth: Keyed by the figma element's orderIndex. A number is the matching web orderIndex; 'missing' = designed but not built; 'decor' = design-only decoration; '?' = undecidable, excluded from scoring.
_pattern: Cards pair with cards and their inner images with images, template index by template index: figma 1/2 -> web 2/3 (tpl 0.0), 3/4 -> 4/5 (0.1), and so on through 0.11. The design carries a THIRTEENTH card (tpl 0.12, figma 33) that the page does not build - the one genuine 'missing'.
_excluded: figma 12 is the purple bullet beside the eyebrow label: visible in the design, but the page has no standalone element for it. figma 26 is the button's text, which the page exposes only as the parent link (figma 24 -> web 26). Both are '?' rather than 'missing' - the ink is on screen, it simply has no separable counterpart.
_webExtra: Structural/layout wrappers rather than designed elements.
_webUnclaimed: Web 12 is neither claimed nor marked extra on the sheet; unclaimed either way, so it does not affect precision.
_note: 28 real matches, 2 excluded as '?', 3 'decor', 1 'missing'. No conflicts.
